scoring_justification: The mean-field spinodal CSV is checked for structural properties (critical temperature within 5% of 1.5J and reentrance of low-density spinodal) because recomputing the full numerical phase diagram in the checker is too heavy. The power-law exponent is a result-level compare to the paper-reported value (-3.5) with tolerance, as recomputing the exponent from raw simulation data is also too heavy.

hidden_assets.purpose: Power-law exponent reference value from paper
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper reports P(n) ~ n^{-3.5} +/- 0.05 (early-time distribution section).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: This is the exact value published in the paper; no fabrication.

outputs.description: Mean-field spinodal and coexistence densities as a function of temperature, computed from the lattice model constitutive relations.
Power-law exponent of the early-time aggregate size distribution, fitted from dynamic Monte Carlo simulation.

output_contract.notes: The mean-field spinodal CSV is checked for structural properties (critical temperature and reentrance) rather than exact numeric match. The power-law exponent is compared to a hidden reference value with an appropriate tolerance.

steps.description: Check critical temperature (where spinodal densities converge) within 5% of 1.5J and verify that the low-density spinodal density at T=0.2J is greater than at T=0.8J (reentrance).
The absolute value of the reported power-law exponent should be 3.5 +/- 0.1.
